theoretical_input.fixed_case: D_eff = J(delta) + downstream optimized loss; original fixed-D theorem is recovered when D_eff is supplied directly
theoretical_input.general_effective_cost: D_eff(delta,C) = J(delta) + min_c [K(c)+M(delta-c)] over 0 <= c <= min(C,delta)
theoretical_input.hidden_state_adaptive: E[J(delta,H)+min_c{K(c,H)+M(delta-c,H)} | I] when compensation may adapt after H is learned
theoretical_input.hidden_state_precommitted: E[J(delta,H)|I] + min_c E[K(c,H)+M(delta-c,H)|I] when one compensation plan must be chosen before H
theoretical_input.compensation_only_special_case: previous expression min_c[K(c)+M(delta-c)] is the exact special case J(delta)=0

direct_empirical_requirements: independently estimated effective waiting cost D_eff for each actor, either as the total causal effect of a biologically faithful waiting intervention or through a preregistered decomposition into direct waiting cost J, raw delay delta, compensatory capacity C, compensation cost K, and residual timing-loss function M
state-mismatch losses C_F and C_M plus prior pi on the same utility scale
observed cue-use decision distinguishing commit-now from wait/use-cue
repeated q support crossing the predicted threshold or pairwise asynchronous window

if compensation occurs in multiple stages, a preregistered causal model must map each stage's recoverable delay and cost into the common D_eff utility scale rather than multiplying observed timing correlations
primary_predictions: D_eff_1 < D_eff_2 implies q_1 < q_2 under shared state-loss structure
Delta q = |D_eff_2-D_eff_1|/(A+L) when both thresholds are finite
actors with equal raw delay can have unequal q thresholds if compensatory capacity or compensation cost differs
exactly one actor uses the shared cue for min(q_1,q_2) < q <= max(q_1,q_2)
complete timing compensation does not imply D_eff=0 when direct nonrecoverable waiting cost J(delta)>0
the constant window-width identity Delta q=|Delta D_eff|/(A+L) is licensed only when actor-specific D_eff is fixed with respect to the focal cue
if the focal cue also informs compensation, actor-specific thresholds must be obtained from V_A(q)=D_eff_i(q), not by plugging a constant D_eff into the fixed-cost formula

inverse_validation.role: infer the effective fitness cost implied by an independently observed behavioral threshold
inverse_validation.strongest_test: compare D_eff_revealed with an independently estimated total causal D_eff or independently reconstructed J+optimized(K+M)
inverse_validation.circularity_guard: cue-use observations used to estimate q_wait may not also define the independent D_eff comparator
inverse_validation.raw_delay_guard: D_eff_revealed must not be compared directly with days delayed, arrival delay, or captivity duration unless the common fitness mapping and treatment fidelity are independently established
inverse_validation.scope: The identity D_eff_revealed=q_wait*(A+L)-max(A,L) identifies the effective cost evaluated at the observed threshold. It can be treated as a cue-independent D_eff only if the focal-cue exogeneity gate passes.
inverse_validation.dual_use_guard: If the focal cue also informs compensation, compare threshold behavior to the dual-use model V_A(q)=D_eff(q); do not interpret D_eff_revealed as a constant actor trait.

greater_snow_goose_status.perturbation_cost: captivity-duration manipulation provides a D-like total perturbation cost but mixes natural waiting with handling/confinement stress; detected breeders showed no clear captivity-duration shift in arrival or laying date
greater_snow_goose_status.timing_loss: Bylot long-term reproductive-success surface provides two-sided C_F-like/C_M-like anchors
greater_snow_goose_status.compensation: 1997-1999 tracking shows later departure associated with shorter migration duration and weak departure-arrival coupling
greater_snow_goose_status.behavioral_uptake: prospective 2019-2023 GPS lane registered but event access requires authenticated Movebank session and exact route geometry
greater_snow_goose_status.clean_D_eff: NOT_IDENTIFIED: neither a biologically faithful waiting total-effect intervention nor a complete J/K/M decomposition is currently available
greater_snow_goose_status.post_arrival_buffering: Bety et al. 2003: lay-date coefficient on relative arrival date 0.45 +/- 0.09 after premigration body-condition control; prelaying duration slope versus arrival -0.53 (R2=0.55); retained as phenomenological buffering only because sequential-timing inference has a published critique
greater_snow_goose_status.direct_waiting_cost: carry-over fitness effects despite little detected timing shift motivate a nonrecoverable J(delta) pathway, but captivity does not identify natural J

promotion_rule: No direct natural D_eff-to-threshold claim until q, D_eff, the common loss scale, and cue-use switching are independently identified in one qualifying system under a pre-outcome contract.

total_effect_route.estimand: D_eff_causal(delta) = E[Y(0)] - E[Y(delta, adapt)] on the common additive fitness-loss scale
total_effect_route.design: randomize or otherwise identify a biologically faithful information-waiting intervention while allowing ordinary downstream compensation
total_effect_route.advantage: directly estimates total effective waiting cost without separately identifying J, K and M
total_effect_route.guard: treatment-specific stress or constraint not intrinsic to natural information waiting identifies the manipulation cost, not natural D_eff

mechanistic_route.design: independently identify direct waiting cost, compensatory capacity, compensation cost and residual timing-loss function
mechanistic_route.advantage: explains why D_eff has its observed value and supports transport across contexts
mechanistic_route.guard: sequential timing correlations alone do not identify causal stage-specific compensation

focal_cue_exogeneity_gate.question: Does the focal cue used to decide whether to wait also change the downstream compensation policy or expected compensation loss conditional on waiting?
fixed_D_eff_allowed_when: D_eff is causally independent of focal cue quality q over the tested range
or downstream compensation is chosen without using the focal cue
or a cue-independent total effective waiting cost has been identified for the relevant decision
dual_use_required_when: the focal cue changes which compensation action is chosen
the focal cue changes expected downstream compensation loss R_C(q)
or D_eff(q) otherwise changes with focal cue quality
focal_cue_exogeneity_gate.dual_use_decision_rule: wait iff V_A(q) > D_eff(q); in the additive binary dual-use special case wait iff V_A(q)+V_C(q) > J+R_C0
